learning_outcomes.text: Identify and explain how to establish, in a CAD system, the graphic elements that make up the general representation norms in industrial technical drawing.
Identify and explain the facilities offered by a CAD system related to the elements that define graphic calculation in industrial technical drawing.
Identify and explain how to establish, in a CAD system, the elements that together constitute the dimensioning module in industrial technical drawing.
Identify and explain how a CAD system facilitates the correct and rapid representation of a part's projections in orthographic view.
Identify and explain the techniques offered by CAD systems regarding the inscription of tolerances and surface finish on technical drawings.
Set up a CAD system for tracing graphic elements related to the general representation norms in industrial technical drawing.
Correctly use the facilities of a CAD system related to graphic calculation in industrial technical drawing.
Set up a CAD system to allow dimensioning according to a specific dimensioning standard.
Correctly use IT technologies such as Polar and Tracking in a CAD system.

Correctly use the facilities offered by CAD systems regarding the inscription of tolerances on technical drawings, as well as those related to surface finish inscription, or create new facilities using the block technique.

Respect principles, norms, and ethical values in the correct and timely execution of professional tasks, by adopting a rigorous, efficient, and responsible work strategy in making decisions for solving assigned tasks.
Integrate into the work group and apply effective work relationship techniques in multidisciplinary teams, at various hierarchical levels.
Continuously inform and document themselves in their own field of activity by adequately using efficient lifelong learning methods and techniques.
Elaborate professional projects in the field of engineering.

syllabus_topics: General presentation. Definition of computer-aided graphics. Object, importance, and history of computer-aided graphics. Presentation and explanation of the graphic screen. Setting the drawing format, choosing measurement units.
Introductory notions. Aids for using the graphic screen. Referring to particular points of objects. Ways to input commands. Ways to select objects. Coordinate systems.

Justification of the method for creating a plane representation. Using specific line types for industrial technical drawing. Layer technique. Drawing line segments, circles, and circular arcs. Deleting parts of an object. Deleting objects. Copying objects.
Part contours. Filleting and chamfering objects.
Dimensioning subroutine. Dimensioning technical drawings. Establishing dimensioning variable values. Dimensioning techniques.
Writing texts. Using the text editor.
Hatching. Establishing the hatching pattern. Hatching technique.
Isometric axonometric representation. Technique of axonometric representations.
Information commands. Establishing the hatching pattern. Hatching technique.
Less commonly used commands.
Introductory notions of technical drawing in a CAD environment. Setting the drawing space. Practicing different types of coordinates. OSNAP modes.
Applications to geometric drawing.
Using layers, line patterns, and colors. Applications to geometric constructions.
Test I: Choosing the drawing space, building layers, using line patterns and colors. Representation of flange-type contours.
Drawing, in triple orthogonal projection, the views for a medium-complexity mechanical part. Using dimensioning. Using line thicknesses. Using POLAR TRACKING technologies.
Axonometric representation, explanations and presentation of an application.
Test 2: Reading a technical drawing. Axonometric representation of a simple part. Data for the bevel gear is given.

Drawing, in triple orthogonal projection, the views, sections and/or, for a mechanical part. The mechanical part can be represented axonometrically on paper or can be natural. Using dimensioning. Using line thicknesses. Using blocks with attributes for obtaining surface finish symbols. Using symbols to indicate deviations from the reciprocal position of the surface.

Test 3 (summative) Representation in triple orthogonal projection of a part. The representation contains at least one section. Symbolizing and noting the section path is required. Dimensioning of the part is imposed and inscription of surface conditions is required.
Retake assignments.
teaching_methods: Explanatory and participatory lectures based on PowerPoint presentations
Presentations containing graphic representations and short text messages
Brief recap of previous course notions at the beginning of each course
Cognitive model based on connectivist learning

assessment_methods.method: Exam/Verification (includes individual/team assignments, a report/case study, formative tests, and a summative test)

assessment_rules: The final evaluation result for a discipline is obtained by considering the scores and weights allocated to each activity within the discipline. Integer grades from 1 to 10 will be awarded, with a grade of 5 certifying the acquisition of minimal learning outcomes for a discipline and the granting of its associated study credits. To pass, students must correctly trace the projections of a mechanical part using a CAD system, with one of the views in section. They must also know and apply basic dimensioning rules in industrial technical drawing within a CAD system, and correctly understand the three-dimensional shape of a mechanical part represented in triple orthogonal projection.
